name: C
shortDescription: A compact, fast systems language that sits close to the hardware. C powers operating systems, embedded firmware and the runtimes of many other languages, and teaches you how memory really works.
highlights: Variables, types, operators and control flow
Functions, pointers, arrays and strings
Structs, dynamic memory and file I/O

name: C++
shortDescription: C with classes, templates and a large standard library. C++ is used for game engines, browsers, trading systems and anything that needs raw speed together with high-level abstractions.
highlights: Classes, constructors, references and RAII
Templates, the STL containers and algorithms
Smart pointers, move semantics and modern C++ features

name: C#
shortDescription: Microsoft's modern, type-safe language for .NET. Build web APIs with ASP.NET Core, desktop apps, games with Unity and cloud services with one productive toolchain.
highlights: Types, classes, records and pattern matching
LINQ, collections and async/await
Building and testing a .NET console and web app

name: Java
shortDescription: A mature, portable, object-oriented language that runs on the JVM. Java powers enterprise back ends, Android apps and big-data tools, and has one of the largest ecosystems in software.
highlights: Syntax, classes, interfaces and generics
Collections, streams, records and exceptions
Modern Java (21 and later) features and tooling

name: Python
shortDescription: A readable, batteries-included language loved by beginners and experts alike. Python drives data science, automation, web back ends and AI with clear, concise syntax.
highlights: Variables, data types, lists, dicts and loops
Functions, modules, classes and error handling
Files, virtual environments and the standard library

name: JavaScript
shortDescription: The language of the web browser and, with Node.js, of servers too. JavaScript adds interactivity to pages and underpins every modern frontend framework.
highlights: Values, functions, scope and closures
Arrays, objects, classes and modules
Asynchronous code with promises and async/await

name: TypeScript
shortDescription: JavaScript with static types. TypeScript catches bugs before you run your code, powers Angular and scales JavaScript projects to large teams.
highlights: Type annotations, interfaces and unions
Generics, narrowing and utility types
Configuring the compiler and typing real projects

name: PHP
shortDescription: A pragmatic server-side language that runs most of the web, including WordPress and Laravel. Modern PHP is typed, fast and object-oriented.
highlights: Syntax, arrays, functions and forms
Classes, namespaces and Composer
Sessions, databases with PDO and security basics

name: Ruby
shortDescription: An elegant, expressive language designed for programmer happiness. Ruby's readable syntax and the Rails framework make it a favourite for web start-ups.
highlights: Blocks, iterators and everything-is-an-object
Classes, modules and mixins
Gems, Bundler and testing with Minitest

name: Go
shortDescription: A simple, compiled language from Google with built-in concurrency. Go is the language of cloud infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes and countless network services.
highlights: Packages, types, slices, maps and structs
Interfaces, errors and the standard library
Goroutines, channels and building a web service

name: Rust
shortDescription: A systems language that guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector. Rust is used for performance-critical services, command-line tools, WebAssembly and embedded code.
highlights: Ownership, borrowing and lifetimes
Enums, pattern matching, traits and generics
Cargo, crates, error handling and concurrency

name: Swift
shortDescription: Apple's modern language for iOS, macOS, watchOS and server apps. Swift is safe by design, fast and expressive, with optionals and value types at its core.
highlights: Optionals, structs, enums and protocols
Closures, generics and error handling
Swift concurrency and a first SwiftUI screen

name: Kotlin
shortDescription: A concise, null-safe JVM language and the official choice for Android. Kotlin interoperates with Java and also targets the browser, native binaries and multiplatform apps.
highlights: Null safety, data classes and extension functions
Collections, lambdas and coroutines
Java interoperability and Android basics

name: Dart
shortDescription: The client-optimised language behind Flutter. Dart compiles to native code and JavaScript, with sound null safety and a familiar C-style syntax.
highlights: Variables, functions, classes and mixins
Null safety, collections and generics
Futures, streams and a first Flutter widget

name: R
shortDescription: A language built for statistics and data visualisation. R's packages, including the tidyverse and ggplot2, make exploring, modelling and plotting data straightforward.
highlights: Vectors, data frames and factors
dplyr and ggplot2 for wrangling and plots
Statistical tests, models and R Markdown reports

name: MATLAB
shortDescription: A numerical computing environment for matrices, signal processing and simulation. MATLAB is widely used in engineering, control systems and research.
highlights: Matrices, indexing and vectorised operations
Scripts, functions and plotting
Toolboxes, Simulink basics and data import

name: Scala
shortDescription: A JVM language that fuses object-oriented and functional programming. Scala powers Apache Spark and large-scale data pipelines.
highlights: Case classes, pattern matching and traits
Immutable collections and higher-order functions
Scala 3 syntax, implicits and a first Spark job

name: Perl
shortDescription: A text-processing powerhouse with unmatched regular expressions. Perl still runs countless scripts, build systems and bioinformatics pipelines.
highlights: Scalars, arrays, hashes and context
Regular expressions and file handling
Modules from CPAN and writing maintainable scripts

name: Lua
shortDescription: A tiny, embeddable scripting language. Lua scripts games such as Roblox and World of Warcraft, the Neovim editor and network software thanks to its speed and small footprint.
highlights: Tables, functions and metatables
Closures, coroutines and modules
Embedding Lua and scripting a host application

name: Haskell
shortDescription: A purely functional, lazily evaluated language with a powerful type system. Haskell changes how you think about programs, side effects and correctness.
highlights: Pure functions, recursion and lazy evaluation
Algebraic data types, type classes and pattern matching
Functors, monads, IO and building with Cabal or Stack

name: Elixir
shortDescription: A functional language on the Erlang VM for fault-tolerant, concurrent systems. Elixir and Phoenix make real-time web applications scale with ease.
highlights: Pattern matching, pipes and immutable data
Processes, GenServers and supervisors
Mix projects, testing with ExUnit and Phoenix basics

name: Erlang
shortDescription: The language built for telecom-grade reliability. Erlang's lightweight processes and supervision trees keep systems running through failures and hot code upgrades.
highlights: Atoms, tuples, lists and pattern matching
Processes, message passing and OTP behaviours
Supervision trees, releases and fault tolerance

name: Objective-C
shortDescription: The original language of iOS and macOS development. Objective-C adds Smalltalk-style messaging to C and still underpins many Apple frameworks and codebases.
highlights: Classes, messages, properties and protocols
Memory management with ARC
Working with Foundation and bridging to Swift

name: Assembly
shortDescription: The human-readable form of machine code. Learning assembly for x86-64 and ARM shows you what compilers generate and how CPUs, registers and the stack really work.
highlights: Registers, instructions and addressing modes
The stack, calling conventions and system calls
Reading compiler output and writing small routines

name: COBOL
shortDescription: The business language that still processes a large share of the world's banking and government transactions. COBOL is verbose, precise and very much alive.
highlights: Program divisions, data definitions and PICTURE clauses
File handling, records and sequential processing
Reading and maintaining existing COBOL programs

name: Fortran
shortDescription: The first high-level language, still unbeaten for numerical and scientific computing. Modern Fortran powers weather models, physics simulations and high-performance computing.
highlights: Modern Fortran syntax, arrays and modules
Numerical precision, loops and array operations
Compiling with gfortran and calling libraries

name: Julia
shortDescription: A high-performance language for scientific computing that reads like Python and runs like C. Julia solves the two-language problem in numerical work.
highlights: Multiple dispatch, types and functions
Arrays, broadcasting and performance tips
Packages, plotting and data analysis

name: F#
shortDescription: A functional-first language for .NET. F# brings immutable data, pattern matching, discriminated unions and type providers to the Microsoft ecosystem.
highlights: Immutable values, records and unions
Pattern matching, pipelines and computation expressions
Interoperating with C# and the .NET libraries

name: Groovy
shortDescription: A dynamic JVM language with a Java-compatible syntax. Groovy scripts Gradle builds and Jenkins pipelines and adds closures and DSLs to Java projects.
highlights: Dynamic typing, closures and collections
GStrings, builders and metaprogramming
Writing Gradle and Jenkins pipeline scripts

name: Bash
shortDescription: The default shell on Linux and macOS. Bash scripting automates builds, deployments and server tasks with pipes, loops and the Unix command-line tools.
highlights: Commands, pipes, redirection and variables
Conditionals, loops, functions and arguments
Text processing with grep, sed and awk

name: PowerShell
shortDescription: Microsoft's object-oriented shell and scripting language. PowerShell automates Windows, Azure and cross-platform administration with cmdlets and object pipelines.
highlights: Cmdlets, the object pipeline and help system
Variables, control flow, functions and modules
Managing files, processes and remote systems

name: Solidity
shortDescription: The language of Ethereum smart contracts. Solidity lets you write contracts, tokens and decentralised applications that run on the Ethereum Virtual Machine.
highlights: Contracts, state, functions and modifiers
Events, inheritance and the ERC-20 standard
Testing and deploying with Hardhat or Foundry

name: SQL
shortDescription: The standard language for querying and shaping relational data. SQL skills transfer across MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SQLite and analytics tools.
highlights: SELECT, filtering, sorting and aggregation
Joins, subqueries and set operations
Creating tables, constraints, indexes and transactions

name: PL/SQL
shortDescription: Oracle's procedural extension to SQL. PL/SQL adds variables, loops, exceptions and stored procedures that run inside the Oracle database.
highlights: Blocks, variables, control flow and cursors
Procedures, functions, packages and triggers
Exception handling and bulk operations

name: T-SQL
shortDescription: Microsoft's procedural SQL dialect for SQL Server and Azure SQL. T-SQL adds control flow, stored procedures, functions, error handling and window functions to SQL.
highlights: Variables, IF/WHILE and temporary tables
Stored procedures, functions and triggers
TRY/CATCH, transactions and query tuning basics
